pages.api:
# API reference

> The stream, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Stream `can.frame/<source>`

`can.frame.v1`, class `stream`. Each record is the JSON of one data frame, at most 512 bytes: `source_id`, `node_id`, `t_ns` (the wall clock when it was read), `seq`, `id` (11 or 29 bits), `ext`, `fd`, `dlc` (0 to 15), `data` (lower-case hex).

## Reading `telemetry/<source>`

`telemetry.v1`: `frames.rx`, `frames.errors`, `bus.off`, `bus.load` (%), `rx.err_counter`, `tx.err_counter`, `rx.dropped`, `stream.seq`.

## stdout report (one per interval)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `iface`, `stream` | string | |
| `frames`, `frames_per_s`, `fd_frames`, `extended_frames` | numbers | in the window |
| `remote_frames_skipped` | number | remote frames seen, not published |
| `bus_load_pct` | number | estimate, see **The bus** |
| `error_frames`, `error_classes`, `bus_off_events` | numbers, object, number | |
| `top_ids` | array | the five busiest ids with their frame counts |
| `controller` | object/null | `state`, `oper`, `bitrate`, `data_bitrate`, `fd`, `listen_only`, `loopback`, `virtual`, error counters |
| `configured_bitrate`, `bitrate_matches` | number, bool/null | null for a virtual interface |
| `kernel_rx_dropped` | number | the interface's `rx_dropped` since start |
| `transmit` | string | always `never` |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `topic`, `seq`, `write_errors`, `error` |
| `error` | string | only with `no_source` |

## Store vector (id 38)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | `frames_per_s` |
| 1 | `bus_load_pct` |
| 2 | `error_frames` |
| 3 | `bus_off` |
| 4 | `rx_error_counter` |
| 5 | `tx_error_counter` |
| 6 | `kernel_rx_dropped` |
| 7 | `bitrate_ok` (1 matches, 0 differs, -1 no controller) |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8072`, continuous mode)

`/status`, `/raw`, `/history`, `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--iface`, `--bitrate`, `--source`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.bus:
# The bus

> What the numbers in the report mean.

## Controller state

`controller.state` is the kernel's: `ERROR-ACTIVE` (normal), `ERROR-WARNING`, `ERROR-PASSIVE` (the error counters passed 127), `BUS-OFF` (passed 255; the controller has left the bus) or `STOPPED` (the interface is down). A virtual interface has none.

`rx_error_counter` and `tx_error_counter` are the controller's own counters. A healthy bus keeps both near zero; a rising receive counter with no transmitter of ours usually means the wrong bit rate, a missing termination, or a stub that is too long.

## Error frames

The kernel reports controller and bus errors as error frames. The cog counts them by class in `error_classes`: `controller`, `protocol`, `transceiver`, `no_ack`, `bus_error`, `lost_arbitration`, `tx_timeout`, `bus_off`, `restarted`. `no_ack` seen by a listen-only node with another sender is normal for a bus with one transmitter and no other receiver.

## Bit rate

`configured_bitrate` is what you told the cog. `controller.bitrate` is what the kernel runs. `bitrate_matches` is false when they differ. A listener at the wrong rate sees only errors.

## Load

`bus_load_pct` counts the bits of the frames seen (47 for a standard header, 67 for an extended, plus 8 per data byte), adds 20% for bit stuffing, and divides by what the bit rate carries in the window. Above 70% sustained is a busy bus.

## CAN FD

Frames up to 64 bytes are published with their length code (`dlc` 0 to 15). The load figure counts FD frames at the nominal rate, which overstates the load of a frame sent with bit-rate switching.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Bring the interface up as the operator, then run the cog.

## Real hardware

The cog never does this; you do:

```
sudo ip link set can0 up type can bitrate 500000            # classic CAN
sudo ip link set can0 up type can bitrate 500000 dbitrate 2000000 fd on     # CAN FD
```

Add `listen-only on` to be sure the controller cannot acknowledge or send. Check with `ip -details link show can0`. Wire the bus through a transceiver, terminate **both** ends with 120 ohms, and keep stubs short.

## Without hardware (a virtual interface)

```
sudo modprobe vcan
sudo ip link add dev vcan0 type vcan
sudo ip link set up vcan0
cog-can-fd --once --iface vcan0 --window 10
```

Undo it with `sudo ip link del vcan0` (and, if nothing else uses it, `sudo modprobe -r vcan`).

## From a shell

```
cog-can-fd --once --iface can0 --bitrate 500000      # listen ten seconds
cog-can-fd --iface can0 --bitrate 500000             # continuous; status on :8072
cog-can-fd --once --simulate                         # synthetic traffic
cog-can-fd --once --replay drive.log                 # a candump -L log
```

## Placed on a node

Place `can-fd` through the controller. Its `cog.toml` declares the interfaces (`[[devices]] netdev = "can*"`), the stream and the telemetry output. The host refuses the placement if another cog owns a CAN interface, and hands the owner the interface names in `WEFTOS_DEVICES`.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Put the frames of a CAN bus where every other cog can read them, and never put one on it.

`can-fd` listens to one SocketCAN interface (`can0`, `vcan0`, ...). Each data frame, classic or CAN FD, becomes a `can.frame.v1` record in the stream `can.frame/<source>`. The report counts frames, error frames by class, bus-off events and the controller's error counters, estimates the bus load, and says whether the interface runs at the bit rate you configured.

## The short path

1. **Know your bus.** Bit rate, classic or FD, termination at both ends. → see **The bus**
2. **Bring the interface up** (an operator step): `sudo ip link set can0 up type can bitrate 500000`. → see **Set up**
3. **Run it.** `cog-can-fd --once --iface can0 --bitrate 500000` listens for ten seconds and prints a report.
4. **Place it.** The host hands it the interface name and nothing else. → see **Set up**

You can test with no bus and no root: `--once --simulate`, a `candump -L` log through `--replay`, or a virtual interface `vcan0`.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- **Receive only.** The cog opens a raw socket and reads. It has no code that writes to the socket. Sending on a bus (actuation) is a separate decision, WeftOS ADR-123, which is not accepted.
- **It does not configure the interface.** A down interface is `no_source` with the reason. Setting a bit rate is the operator's, because a wrong rate can disturb a live bus.
- **Remote frames are counted, not published.** `can.frame.v1` has no place for them.
- **Timestamps are the wall clock when the frame was read**, not the controller's hardware stamp, so they carry scheduling jitter of a millisecond or so.
- **One interface per cog.** The cog claims every CAN interface on the node (`can*`) and reads one of them.
- The load figure is an estimate: bits of the frames seen, plus 20% for bit stuffing, over what the bit rate carries.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

| `error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `the interface is down` | `ip link ... up` has not been done | bring it up as the operator (see **Set up**) |
| `the controller is bus-off` | the controller left the bus after errors | check bit rate, termination, wiring; restart the interface |
| `ip link show ...` | the interface does not exist | check the name; for a virtual one, create it |
| `socket(PF_CAN ...)` | the `can_raw` module is not loaded | `sudo modprobe can_raw` |
| `no CAN interface in WEFTOS_DEVICES` | the host handed no interface | place through the controller or pass `--iface` |

## Frames arrive but `error_frames` grows

Read `error_classes`. `bus_error` and `protocol` with a rising `rx_error_counter`: wrong bit rate or bad wiring. `no_ack` with a quiet bus: only one node on the bus, which cannot acknowledge itself.

## `bitrate_matches` is false

The interface runs at a different rate than **Configured bit rate**. Fix whichever is wrong; the cog changes neither.

## `kernel_rx_dropped` grows

The socket buffer overflowed: the cog was not scheduled in time, or the bus load is very high. Lower the other load on the node.

## No frames and no errors

The bus is silent, or the cog listens to the wrong interface. Check `iface` in the report and `candump` on the same interface.

toml:
# Sensor guide for can-fd (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md).

schema = 1
title = "A CAN bus on a Linux board"
sensor = "CAN / CAN FD controller exposed as a SocketCAN interface"
cog = "can-fd"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "bus", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
bus = "bus"
interface_up = "setup"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "CAN bus"
detail = "transceiver, wiring, termination"

[[flow]]
name = "SocketCAN"
detail = "canX, bit rate set by the operator"

[[flow]]
name = "can-fd cog"
detail = "receive only, error classes, load"

[[flow]]
name = "Outputs"
detail = "can.frame stream, telemetry, :8072"
